title: You are fired with no warning
lede: You are called into a room at 10am. HR is already sitting there, which tells you the decision was made before you walked in. Someone says the words "we have decided to let you go." Your ears get hot and the rest of the sentence arrives as noise.

blocks.text: You are called into a room at 10am. HR is already sitting there, which tells you the decision was made before you walked in. Someone says the words "we have decided to let you go." Your ears get hot and the rest of the sentence arrives as noise.

items: Nothing you say in this room will reverse the decision. It was made days ago, signed off by people who are not present, and the meeting exists to deliver it and to document that it was delivered. Arguing your value here is spending energy on a locked door.

What is still live is everything financial and procedural: your final pay, your notice, your unused leave, your equity, your reference, your health cover, what they will tell people, and whether you leave with dignity. Those are decided in the next ten days, not in the last ten seconds of this meeting.

They expect one of three reactions — collapse, rage, or begging. A fourth reaction, calm procedural competence, reliably produces better terms, because it signals that you will read what they send you.

items.move: Say almost nothing for the first minute
items.detail: Let them finish. Do not fill the silence. The silence is uncomfortable for them, not for you, and people who are uncomfortable offer things.
Last day. Final pay date and what it includes. Notice or pay in lieu. Whether this is redundancy, dismissal, or resignation on paper — the word chosen changes your rights and what you can claim.
Especially not a settlement, waiver, or "mutual separation" document. Say you will review it. Signing in the room is the single most expensive mistake available to you.
Every term they just said out loud. If a manager promised a good reference or an extra month, that promise evaporates the moment they change jobs unless it is in an email.

items.move: Secure your own material before you lose access
items.detail: Your contract, payslips, reviews, commendations, your contacts list, anything you are legally entitled to. Not company data — yours. Access is usually cut within the hour.
The story colleagues tell about your exit becomes your informal reference in the industry for years. Ninety seconds of dignity is worth more than any parting line.

items.say: "I want to make sure I understand this properly rather than react. Can you put the terms in writing and I will come back with questions?"
"Is this being recorded as redundancy or dismissal? I need to know which, for my own records."
"I do not sign documents I have not read. I will review it and respond by Thursday."
"Can we agree the wording of my reference now, in writing, while we are both being reasonable about this?"

items: Signing the settlement in the room because the number sounds large and you feel humiliated.
Arguing your performance record. It converts a procedural meeting into a fight you cannot win.
Sending the honest email to the whole company. It feels like justice for about four hours.
Telling them you will get a lawyer if you have not decided to. Threats you do not act on teach them your threats are noise.
Deleting or taking company files as leverage. That turns your grievance into their case.
Write down exactly what was said, who was there, and the date, while it is fresh. This document is worth more than your memory in six weeks.
Work out your actual runway in months — cash, obligations, the real number. Fear shrinks dramatically once it becomes arithmetic.
Have the settlement read by someone who does this professionally if the sum is meaningful. One hour of advice routinely moves these numbers.
Tell people you trust within two days. Isolation after a firing does more damage than the firing.
Build your version of the story in one calm paragraph before interviews force you to improvise it.

limit: If the dismissal followed you reporting wrongdoing, taking medical or parental leave, or is tied to your race, sex, age, disability, religion, or pregnancy, stop handling this alone. That is a protected-grounds case with deadlines measured in weeks. Get employment advice before you sign anything.
